title: The unit sublist of generators generates the unit group
statement: Let $P$ be a fine commutative monoid, written additively, and choose a finite monoid generating list $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Write $G=P^{\rm gp}$ for its group completion [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and identify $P\subseteq G$. Put $U=P^\times=\{u\in P:-u\in P\}$ and $I=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,d\}:a_i\in U\}$. In every expression $u=\sum_{i=1}^d n_i a_i$ with $u\in U$ and $n_i\in\mathbf N$, $n_i>0$ implies $i\in I$. The submonoid of $P$ generated by $\{a_i:i\in I\}$ is exactly $U$. Consequently $U$ is a finitely generated abelian group. Moreover, if $G$ is torsion free, then $U$ is torsion free as well: for $u\in U$ and $n>0$, $nu=0$ implies $u=0$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.3 and 3.1.11, printed pp.98,100; agent algebraic refinement: the finite unit-generating-sublist argument from old step 6. No claim that ILO states this auxiliary lemma verbatim.

proof.text: For an expression u = product_i a_i ^ n_i with u a unit, Mathlib IsUnit.prod_univ_iff shows that each a_i ^ n_i is a unit. For n_i > 0, isUnit_pow_iff then makes a_i a unit. These statements hold in every commutative monoid and avoid the explicit completion calculation of the original proof.

Let S be the submonoid closure of the unit generators. All its generators are units, so S is contained in IsUnit.submonoid P. For the reverse inclusion use closure induction on membership in closure(range a), which is top by ha, with the predicate IsUnit x implies x belongs to S. At a generator this is subset_closure; at 1 it is one_mem; at a product x*y the commuting-product unit criterion makes x and y units separately, and the induction hypotheses and mul_mem finish. This includes the empty generating list and empty unit sublist.

The unit-generator set is finite as the image of a subset of Fin d. Step 2 and Submonoid.fg_iff give finite generation of IsUnit.submonoid P. The image of the top submonoid of P-units under Units.coeHom is exactly that submonoid. Its injectivity (Units.val_injective) and Submonoid.FG.map_injective give monoid finite generation of P-units. Group.fg_iff_monoid_fg converts this into the stated group finite generation.

Use fineness [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] for injectivity of the canonical map to the group completion [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. If u^n=1 in P-units and n>0, apply the value map and the canonical completion homomorphism to get of(u)^n=1. Mathlib pow_eq_one_iff_left in the torsion-free completion gives of(u)=1. Injectivity gives the value of u equal to 1, and Units.ext gives u=1.
